newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Gunmen execute six in Taiwan official's home.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen execute six in Taiwan official's home.

text.p: Gunmen burst into a Taiwan county official's home on Thursday and shot nine people in the head after tying them up, killing six and critically wounding three, police said.
Taoyuan county magistrate Liu Pang-yu was listed in hospital in very critical condition, a police spokesman in the northern Taiwan county told Reuters.
The gunmen escaped and were being hunted by police.
Premier Lien Chan ordered Taiwan's air and seaports to conduct stepped up checks of all departing passengers.

State television reporters at the scene quoted investigators as saying at least two gunmen burst into Liu's home on Thursday morning, bound the hands of Liu and eight others and systematically shot each in the head at close range.
The motive for the shooting was not known.
Aside from magistrate Liu, the victims also included a county council member, two security guards, a driver, a secretary and Liu's brother.
The state-run Central News Agency, without citing a source, said it could be related to a local property development case.
State radio reports suggested the shooting could be related to Taiwan's underworld. Gangsters have long infiltrated Taiwan's political and financial world.
President Lee Teng-hui's office issued a statement calling for speedy police work.
"President Lee is extremely shocked," the statement said. "He has ordered related government agencies to solve the case as soon as possible."
